jurisdictions.jurisdiction: Honolulu County, HI (City & County of Honolulu)
jurisdictions.notes: HI's top county by population, no config wired. DPP's live system (HNL Build/CivCheck AI) is an interactive web portal only, no public API (SODA/REST/OData) -- confirmed by Gemini on a direct feedback round after being shown the staleness evidence (this time gave an honest 'no active API exists' answer instead of guessing). No ArcGIS FeatureServer for permits either (HoLIS only has zoning/TMK/parcel layers). Would require either a UIPA public-records request or scraping HNL Build's UI directly -- not attempted, out of scope for now (not a CAPTCHA/anti-bot case, just genuinely no queryable feed).

Default 'Building' module 404s here; real vertical-construction permits live under the 'PublicWorks' module's search form (record type PublicWorks/Building/Commercial/New Building, visible label 'BUILDING COMMERCIAL NEW BUILDING') -- confirmed live by fetching the module's real dropdown option HTML. 180-day window: 190 fetched, 180 new after merge.

Fulton is GA's actual top county by population (Gwinnett, already wired, is #2). Fulton county govt issues almost no permits itself (nearly 100% incorporated into Atlanta/Sandy Springs/Roswell/etc) -- City of Atlanta carries the vast majority of volume. Accela agency code 'ATLANTA_GA' verified live (200 on Welcome.aspx), real Building module dropdown confirmed 20+ Commercial-prefixed record types. 180-day window: 91 fetched, 81 new after merge.

Louisville Metro is a consolidated city-county government, so this genuinely covers the whole county. Gemini's answer was unusually accurate (dataset name + full field schema all matched exactly) but didn't give the real service URL -- found via ArcGIS Online item search + item-info lookup. MAX(ISSUE_DATE)=2026-07-28 (today, exceptionally fresh), CATEGORY_NAME='Commercial' real (888 total rows; other values Single Family/Multifamily/Condo-Patio/null). 180-day window: 77 fetched, 77 new.

Portland Permitting & Development does NOT use Accela -- publishes directly via PortlandMaps ArcGIS REST. Layer name is literally 'Commercial Construction Permit', pre-filtered by the city itself (same pattern as MD-MONTGOMERY), no where-clause needed. MAX(ISSUED)=2026-07-24, 7,071 total rows. 180-day window: 75 fetched, only 1 new -- most already captured by earlier manual research.

Genuine dead end -- CT abolished county government entirely in 1960, no unified building department exists. Checked all major municipalities (Stamford, Bridgeport, Norwalk, Fairfield town, Greenwich): all use proprietary platforms (OpenGov/ViewPoint Cloud, CitySquared) with zero public API access, no Accela deployment anywhere in the county. State-level data.ct.gov only has aggregated annual town-level housing permit counts, not row-level transactional data. Honest Gemini answer, no fabrication -- ruled out.
